TPS3808G01 command qualification timer. CT connected to VDD through 49.9k gives 180/300/420 ms release delay after ZERO_RAW rises. MR going low resets immediately; no passive diode residual/stale RC permission. SENSE directly monitors VDD >0.405 V; separate G33 supervisor enforces valid logic supply.

Condition wired comparator fault into a guaranteed low logic level. MR VIL=0.3VDD accommodates TLV170x low output <=0.9 V only while valid 3.3 V rail is above supervisor threshold. Output asserts after MR propagation, nominal 150 ns, then releases 12..28 ms after raw fault clears. No guaranteed maximum fault latency is claimed.

sequence: FAULT_N low clears ARMED. The coil deenergizes and the AND gate forces AMP_ARMED low.
An explicit ARM edge after the core is healthy sets ARMED. The coil energizes immediately; AMP_ARMED remains low.
After a 12 to 28 ms delay, AMP_ARMED goes high. Relay operate time including bounce is 1 ms maximum under the manufacturer's stated conditions.

C1 qualifies a near-zero command when the ARM edge is accepted. Keep command zero throughout the 12 to 28 ms relay-settle delay and until amplifier enable. There is no independent continuous zero-command hold throughout this interval.
A new fault drives AMP_ARMED low without the turn-on delay. OPA462 disable is 4 microseconds typical. Actual relay release and coil-clamp transients require measurement.
validation_remaining: Verify coil operate/release at actual regulated 5 V and temperature. The manufacturer's operate-time conditions must hold before comparing the 1 ms maximum to the 12 ms minimum delay.
Measure COIL_LOW peak below 26 V and actual relay release. No relay inductance or guaranteed TVS energy has been assumed. Keep the TVS, MOSFET and coil-return loop short.

Place a 10 kilohm E/D pulldown at the amplifier itself so detaching its enable wire forces off.
Open relay contacts do not discharge external stored charge. Any external bleeder changes the waveform and current budget and must be specified separately.
